correctness.rationale: The nonnegative Hamiltonian identity characterizes exactly the ground configurations: two opposite pure parts and one free part. Interior cube vertices have no inter-cube flip; junctions belong to two cubes. Each allowed edge has conductance 1/2 with counting speed measure. The cube Walsh eigenvalues are |S|, so on the mean-zero space the two antipodal evaluation representers have diagonal 2^{-n} sum_{k>=1} binom(n,k)/k and off-diagonal -2^{-n}H_n. The latter follows by binomial integration, and concentration of a Bin(n,1/2) variable, expanding 1/k around n/2 off the exponentially small tails, yields the diagonal 2/n(1+O(1/n)). Inverting the two-point Gram matrix gives the claimed sharp quadratic cost. Summing it and minimizing over each common endpoint gives n/4 times the cycle difference form to relative o(1); choosing the endpoint averages attains this precision. Cube Poincare bounds the total within-cube variance by the energy, while the six eliminated duplicate junction squares are O(sum m_j^2 + E/n) by the Green bound. The full squared norm is therefore 2^n sum m_j^2 + O(E + sum m_j^2). The six-dimensional trial space and the lower bound on the resulting low eigenspace give the six-mode min–max limit; more directly, any seven-dimensional space meets the zero-cube-mean kernel, on which E >= ||f||^2, proving lambda_6 >= 1 whenever that eigenvalue exists. For passage, the conductance across radial shells k,k+1 is (n-k)binom(n,k)/2. Series/parallel reduction and N=6(2^n-1) times resistance give the commute time; reflection halves it. The exact formula works also at n=1, where the graph is already the six-cycle. The reciprocal-binomial sum tends to 2. Verification files were inspected, not executed. The separate /workspace/branches/review-replay.py checks all distances on the unreduced flip graph at n=1,2,4,8 and its smallest eigenvalues at n=2,4,8; this is corroboration only.
